atlas.crises.ai2026.cause: Hyperscaler AI capex (~$1tn 2025–26) outpacing free cash flow, record concentration (Mag-7 ≈ 35% of the S&P 500) and CAPE ≈ 41 — the BIS (28 Jun 2026), ECB FSR (27 May 2026), Fed FSR (8 May 2026) and Bank of England all warn of a possible sharp correction; econometric bubble tests are split (Cowles/Yale GSADF finds explosiveness; a 2026 counter-paper finds none once tech fundamentals are modeled).
atlas.crises.ai2026.highlight: Institutional + algorithmic verdict: GOLD is elevated to lead regime-matched hedge — 2026 hedge score 0.85, a statistical co-lead with phase-1 cash (0.88), decisively above 'challenged' Treasuries (0.42). Basis: 27% of global reserves vs 22% UST (ECB, 2 Jun 2026), regime-match r 0.96–0.98 with monetary-crisis scripts, worst-quintile beta ≈ 0, and gold Granger-LEADS the market this cycle. Caveat: a +130% run-up means part of the hedge is pre-paid. CHF secondary; the yen (~¥162) and Bitcoin (−51% from ATH) look falsified this cycle.
atlas.crises.ai2026.sources: BIS Annual Economic Report 2026; ECB FSR May 2026 & Int'l Role of the Euro Jun 2026; Fed FSR May 2026; BoE FSR 2026; WGC Jun 2026; Duffie (2020)
atlas.crises.depression.cause: Equity bubble, banking collapse and deflation. Dow −89% peak-to-trough (Jul 1932).
atlas.crises.depression.highlight: Homestake Mining +474–580% while the Dow lost 89% — the archetypal crisis-unique winner under the fixed gold price.
atlas.crises.depression.sources: Brunnermeier & Oehmke (2013); Jordà et al. (2019) QJE; economic-history literature on gold-standard mining shares
atlas.crises.stagflation.cause: Growth-stock overvaluation meets oil shock and inflation. S&P 500 −48%; Nifty Fifty names fell 70–90%.
atlas.crises.stagflation.highlight: Gold ≈ +385% within the window (post-Bretton-Woods repricing); crude roughly QUADRUPLED after the Oct 1973 embargo ($2.90 → $11.65/bbl — the highest-magnitude crisis-unique winner, Alpanda & Peralta-Alva 2010); collateralized commodity futures roughly doubled (Gorton & Rouwenhorst 2006).
atlas.crises.stagflation.sources: Gorton & Rouwenhorst (2006) FAJ; Alpanda & Peralta-Alva (2010) Rev. Econ. Dynamics; Erb & Harvey (2013); Siegel (1998); Fesenmaier & Smith (2002)
atlas.crises.japan.cause: Monetary over-expansion, land + equity bubble. Nikkei −80% by 2003 (decline continues beyond this window).
atlas.crises.japan.highlight: Deflation made JGBs and the yen the standout winners; rolling Nikkei puts are the stylized crisis-unique convexity trade.
atlas.crises.japan.sources: Ranaldo & Söderlind (2010) Rev. Finance; Brunnermeier & Oehmke (2013)
atlas.crises.blackmonday.cause: Portfolio insurance and market microstructure. Dow −22.6% in a single day; ≈ −33% intra-quarter.
atlas.crises.blackmonday.highlight: Gold was a weak-to-strong safe haven for the US and Canada (Baur & McDermott 2010); Treasuries and the yen rallied.
atlas.crises.blackmonday.sources: Baur & McDermott (2010) J. Banking & Finance; Ranaldo & Söderlind (2010)
atlas.crises.asia.cause: USD-pegged EM currency and credit bust. Thai equities ≈ −80% in USD terms; Indonesian GNP −84% in USD.
atlas.crises.asia.highlight: The US dollar was the classic EM-crisis winner (+~115% vs THB at the extreme); gold rose in local-currency terms.
atlas.crises.asia.sources: Reinhart & Rogoff (2009); safe-haven currency literature (Ranaldo & Söderlind 2010)
atlas.crises.dotcom.cause: TMT equity bubble (GSADF-dated explosive episode). NASDAQ −78% peak-to-trough (Oct 2002).
atlas.crises.dotcom.highlight: Value's revenge: Fama-French small-value ≈ +16.2%/yr 2000–07 vs S&P +1.7%/yr. Gold FELL — the key exception that demotes it from universal status.
atlas.crises.dotcom.sources: Phillips, Wu & Yu (2011); Fama-French portfolio evidence; Baur & McDermott (2010)
atlas.crises.gfc.cause: US housing / credit bubble and securitization. S&P 500 −57%; real house prices −35% over ~6 years.
atlas.crises.gfc.highlight: The full safe-haven set fired at once: gold strong safe haven at the peak (Baur & McDermott), Treasuries rallied hard, yen appreciated, trend-following delivered crisis alpha, long volatility paid out.
atlas.crises.gfc.sources: Baur & McDermott (2010); Baele et al. (2020) RFS; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) JFE; St. Louis Fed
atlas.crises.euro.cause: Bank–sovereign doom loop; periphery yields spiked to unsustainable levels. Euro-area bank equity collapsed.
atlas.crises.euro.highlight: Core Bunds and US Treasuries rallied; the CHF surged +~50% vs EUR until the SNB floor (Sep 2011); gold in EUR peaked with the crisis.
atlas.crises.euro.sources: Ranaldo & Söderlind (2010); SNB-floor literature; Baele et al. (2020)
atlas.crises.covid.cause: Exogenous pandemic shock + dash-for-cash. S&P 500 −34% in one month — then the fastest recovery on record.
atlas.crises.covid.highlight: Phase 1 was a 'dash for cash': in mid-March even Treasuries sold off while T-bills/money-market funds absorbed record inflows (Duffie 2020) — then duration rallied. Treasuries later failed in the 2022 inflation regime; Bitcoin fell in lockstep with equities: falsified as a safe haven (Conlon & McGee 2020).
atlas.crises.covid.sources: Conlon & McGee (2020) Finance Research Letters; Duffie (2020) Brookings; Corbet et al. (2020); Baele et al. (2020)
atlas.crises.southsea.cause: Debt-for-equity conversion scheme fuelled by credit; shares rose ~8× in six months, then collapsed ~85%.
atlas.crises.southsea.highlight: Hoare's Bank rode the bubble knowingly and exited near the top — IRR ≈ 51% p.a. (Temin & Voth 2004). The winning asset was the timed exit to cash and quality, not the bubble itself.
atlas.crises.southsea.sources: Temin & Voth (2004) AER; Garber (1990 JEP; 2000 MIT Press)
atlas.matrix.gold.depression: Rose via gold-mining shares (Homestake +474–580%) under the fixed gold price.
atlas.matrix.gold.blackmonday: Spiked intraday on Black Monday (+4.2%) then sold off as investors liquidated for cash — an 'ATM' in acute liquidity crunches; weak-to-strong per Baur & McDermott (2010).
atlas.matrix.gold.asia: Rose in local-currency terms as EM currencies collapsed.
atlas.matrix.gold.dotcom: Fell ≈ −27% into the peak and stayed weak — the key exception that demotes gold from universal status.
atlas.matrix.gold.gfc: Strong safe haven at the crisis peak (Baur & McDermott 2010).
atlas.matrix.gold.ai2026: ELEVATED to lead regime-matched hedge: 2026 hedge score 0.85 (co-lead with cash at 0.88) — regime-match r 0.96–0.98 vs monetary-crisis scripts, worst-quintile beta ≈ 0, Granger-leads the market; 27% of global reserves, overtaking US Treasuries at 22% (ECB, 2 Jun 2026); record central-bank demand (WGC, Jun 2026). Caveat: ~$4,100 after the $5,595 Jan-2026 record — part of the hedge is pre-paid.
atlas.matrix.bonds.stagflation: Collapsed in real terms — bonds fail in inflationary regimes.
atlas.matrix.bonds.euro: Core Bunds/Treasuries only; periphery sovereigns were the collapsing asset.
atlas.matrix.bonds.covid: Rallied in the crash, then fell ≈ −25% in the 2022 inflation regime.
atlas.matrix.bonds.ai2026: Challenged: in April 2025 Treasuries, USD and equities fell TOGETHER; BIS (Sep 2025) found Treasury safe-haven correlations near zero since. 2026 hedge score 0.42 — demoted to 5th, behind CHF, for this configuration (Cheema, Ryan & Sarwar 2025: bonds work best in macro/financial downturns, weaker in geopolitical/inflation shocks).
atlas.matrix.cash.depression: Deflation lifted the real value of cash ~25% peak-to-trough.
atlas.matrix.cash.stagflation: Positive nominal T-bill yields but negative real returns in the inflationary regime.
atlas.matrix.cash.covid: March 2020 'dash for cash': even Treasuries sold off while T-bills and money-market funds absorbed record inflows (Duffie 2020; BIS Bulletin No. 2).
atlas.matrix.cash.ai2026: The live phase-1 haven: money-market fund assets at a record $7.95tn (ICI, 1 Jul 2026). 2026 hedge score 0.88 — rank #1 on CERTAINTY (100% worst-month hit rate, no drawdown, par entry); gold is the payoff co-lead.
atlas.matrix.jpy.gfc: Appreciated ≈ +23% vs USD through the acute phase (Ranaldo & Söderlind 2010).
atlas.matrix.jpy.ai2026: ~¥162 — a ~40-year low; carry dominates haven flows, so the yen has NOT behaved as a haven this cycle.
atlas.matrix.chf.euro: +~50% vs EUR until the SNB imposed the 1.20 floor in Sep 2011.
atlas.matrix.chf.ai2026: Credible secondary haven — the franc strengthened materially vs USD 2021–26 (USD/CHF ~0.76 in Jan 2026).
atlas.matrix.usd.asia: The classic EM-crisis winner: +~115% vs THB at the extreme.
atlas.matrix.usd.covid: Spiked in the Mar 2020 dash-for-cash funding stress.
atlas.matrix.usd.ai2026: Worst first half since 1973 in H1 2025 (DXY −10.8%); reserve diversification away from USD documented (ECB, WGC).
atlas.matrix.commodities.stagflation: Equity-like returns, negatively correlated with stocks, positively with inflation (Gorton & Rouwenhorst 2006).
atlas.matrix.oil.stagflation: Crude roughly quadrupled after the Oct 1973 embargo ($2.90 → $11.65/bbl by Jan 1974) — the highest-magnitude crisis-unique winner (Alpanda & Peralta-Alva 2010, Rev. Econ. Dynamics; Fed History).
atlas.matrix.oil.gfc: Fell from ~$147 to ~$34 in the demand-driven collapse (Hamilton 2009, BPEA) — high uniqueness, low recurrence.
atlas.matrix.value.dotcom: Small-value ≈ +16.2%/yr 2000–07 vs S&P +1.7%/yr — the post-bubble rotation.
atlas.matrix.value.gfc: Fell with the market during the crash itself; the premium is post-trough.
atlas.matrix.value.ai2026: The dot-com analogue: value / equal-weight rotation is the leading candidate post-bubble winner if an AI unwind mirrors 2000–02.
atlas.matrix.quality.gfc: QMJ shows mild positive convexity — benefits from flight to quality (Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2019).
atlas.matrix.trend.blackmonday: Crisis alpha is strongest in prolonged drawdowns, weaker in one-day crashes (Kaminski).
atlas.matrix.trend.gfc: +14–18% in 2008 while equities halved (time-series momentum, Moskowitz et al. 2012).
atlas.matrix.vol.blackmonday: Via index puts / portfolio hedges — VIX futures only tradable since 2004, VIX options since 2006.
atlas.matrix.vol.gfc: Long VIX futures/calls materially cut portfolio risk in 2008 (Szado 2009); VIX a stronger US hedge than gold (Hood & Malik 2013). Cost: persistently negative carry (Carr & Wu 2009).
atlas.matrix.vol.ai2026: Convex insurance is available and relatively cheap pre-spike; expected carry is negative between crises (Dew-Becker et al. 2017).
atlas.matrix.btc.covid: Fell in lockstep with the S&P 500; a 10% allocation raised 1% portfolio VaR by 13.6% (Conlon & McGee 2020) — falsified as a safe haven.
atlas.matrix.btc.ai2026: −51% from the Oct 2025 ATH (~$126k) to ~$62k by Jul 2026 while equity indices set records — again trading as a risk asset.
atlas.classification.universal.0: PHASE 1 · Cash / T-bills / USD liquidity — the first-response winner: flight to liquidity and record money-market inflows (Longstaff 2004; Nagel 2016; Krishnamurthy & Vissing-Jorgensen 2012; Baele et al. 2020; Duffie 2020 'dash for cash')
atlas.classification.universal.1: PHASE 2 · Long safe sovereign bonds — 9/10 crises once funding stress eases; best in macro/financial downturns, weaker in geopolitical/inflation shocks (Cheema, Ryan & Sarwar 2025) and challenged since April 2025
atlas.classification.universal.2: Long volatility / index puts — paid in every observed crisis; negative expected carry between crises (Szado 2009; Carr & Wu 2009)
atlas.classification.universal.3: Trend-following / CTA — 'crisis alpha' in prolonged drawdowns (weaker in one-day crashes)
atlas.classification.universal.4: Gold is near-universal but demoted historically (it fell in the dot-com bust) — yet for the 2026 configuration it is ELEVATED to lead regime-matched hedge, score 0.85 co-lead with cash (see Analytics ranking)
atlas.classification.category.0: Gold → monetary / inflation / currency crises — AND 'black-swan' ambiguity: investors buy gold on ambiguous signals, bonds on extreme-but-clear ones (Baur & McDermott 2012 working paper; Caballero & Krishnamurthy 2008)
atlas.classification.category.1: Value / small-value stocks → after equity-growth bubbles (dot-com)
atlas.classification.category.2: US dollar → EM and global funding-stress crises (Asia ’97, LTCM, 2008, 2020)
atlas.classification.category.3: Government bonds → deflationary crises specifically — they are the collapsing asset in sovereign/inflation crises
atlas.classification.category.4: Quality / low-beta → recessionary equity drawdowns generally
atlas.classification.unique.0: Oil / energy — 1973–74: crude ~4× post-embargo; the highest-MAGNITUDE unique winner, though the crisis TYPE recurs (1979, 1990, 2022) and oil FELL in the 2008/2020 demand collapses (Hamilton 2009)
atlas.classification.unique.1: Homestake Mining & gold miners — 1930s: >500% Oct 1929–Dec 1935 vs a ~⅔ Dow loss (Burdekin & Weidenmier 2004) — the most NON-REPLICABLE winner (fixed-gold-price regime)
atlas.classification.unique.3: Mega-cap tech — the COVID recovery trade, not the crash hedge
atlas.classification.unique.4: Hoare's Bank timed exit — South Sea 1720 (IRR ≈ 51% p.a., Temin & Voth 2004)
atlas.classification.falsified.0: Bitcoin — fell in lockstep with equities in Mar 2020 (Conlon & McGee 2020); by Jul 2026 down ~51% from its ATH while indices set records
atlas.classification.falsified.1: Japanese yen (this cycle) — ~¥162, a ~40-year low despite repeated risk episodes; carry has dominated haven flows 2021–26
